title.zh: 卷二十八 唐臣傳第十六: 豆盧革 盧程 任圜 趙鳳 李襲吉 張憲 蕭希甫 劉贊 何瓚
title.en: Volume 28 Later Tang Biographies 8: Dou Luge, Lu Cheng, Ren Huan, Zhao Feng, Li Xiji, Zhang Xian, Xiao Xifu, Liu Zan, He Zan
title.raw: 卷二十八 唐臣傳第十六: 豆盧革 盧程 任圜 趙鳳 李襲吉 張憲 蕭希甫 劉贊 何瓚 Volume 28 Later Tang Biographies 8: Dou Luge, Lu Cheng, Ren Huan, Zhao Feng, Li Xiji, Zhang Xian, Xiao Xifu, Liu Zan, He Zan

sentences.zh: 豆盧革

translations.literal: Dou Luge
translations.idiomatic: Dou Luge

sentences.zh: 豆盧革，父瓚，唐舒州刺史。

translations.literal: Dou Luge—his father Zan had been Tang prefect of Shu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Luge’s father Zan had served Tang as prefect of Shu.

sentences.zh: 豆盧為世名族，唐末天下亂，革避地之中山，唐亡，為王處直掌書記。

translations.literal: The Dou Lu were a famous clan of the age. At the end of Tang, when the realm was in chaos, Ge took refuge in Zhongshan. After Tang fell he served Wang Chuzhi as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: The Dou Lu were a great house. When Tang collapsed into chaos, Ge fled to Zhongshan. After the dynasty fell he became chief secretary to Wang Chuzhi.

sentences.zh: 莊宗在魏，議建唐國，而故唐公卿之族遭亂喪亡且盡，以革名家子，召為行臺左丞相。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong was in Wei, they debated establishing the Tang state. Former Tang aristocratic clans had perished in the chaos nearly to extinction. Because Ge was a scion of a famous house, he was summoned as Left Chancellor of the Field Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong was at Wei, planning to raise Tang again. The old Tang nobility had been wiped out in the wars. Ge, a famous name, was called to serve as Left Chancellor of the Field Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 莊宗即位，拜同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne, Ge was appointed Co-Signatory of the Secretariat and Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhuangzong’s accession Ge became Co-Signatory of the Secretariat and Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 革雖唐名族，而素不學問，除拜官吏，多失其序，常為尚書郎蕭希甫駁正，革頗患之。

translations.literal: Although Ge was of a famous Tang clan, he had never studied. In appointing officials he often got the order wrong and was frequently corrected by Attendant Secretary Xiao Xifu. Ge resented this deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Ge came from a great Tang clan but had no learning. His appointments were often out of order, and Attendant Secretary Xiao Xifu kept correcting him. Ge hated it.

sentences.zh: 莊宗已滅梁，革乃薦韋說為相。

translations.literal: After Zhuangzong had destroyed Liang, Ge recommended Wei Shuo as chief councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Once Liang was destroyed, Ge put forward Wei Shuo as chief councillor.

sentences.zh: 說，唐末為殿中侍御史，坐事貶南海，後事梁為禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Shuo had served in late Tang as palace attendant censor, was demoted to the South Seas for an offense, and later served Liang as vice-minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo had been a palace censor under late Tang, was banished to the South Seas for a crime, and later served Liang as vice-minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 革以說能知前朝事，故引以佐己，而說亦無學術，徒以流品自高。

translations.literal: Ge brought Shuo in because Shuo knew former-court affairs and could assist him, but Shuo too had no learning and merely flaunted his pedigree.
translations.idiomatic: Ge wanted Shuo for his knowledge of the old court, but Shuo was no scholar either—he only traded on birth.

sentences.zh: 是時，莊宗內畏劉皇后，外惑宦官、伶人，郭崇韜雖盡忠於國，而亦無學術，革、說俯仰默默無所為，唯諾崇韜而已。

translations.literal: At that time Zhuangzong feared Empress Liu within and was swayed by eunuchs and actors outside. Guo Chongtao was loyal to the state but likewise had no learning. Ge and Shuo bowed and kept silent, doing nothing but assenting to Chongtao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong feared Empress Liu at home and listened to eunuchs and actors abroad. Chongtao was loyal but unlearned. Ge and Shuo nodded along and did nothing but agree with him.

sentences.zh: 唐、梁之際，仕宦遭亂奔亡，而吏部銓文書不完，因緣以為奸利，至有私鬻告敕，亂易昭穆，而季父、母舅反拜侄、甥者，崇韜請論以法。

translations.literal: Between Tang and Liang, officials fled the chaos, and the Ministry of Personnel’s appointment records were incomplete. People exploited this for profit—even selling appointment edicts privately, scrambling genealogical ranks so that uncles and maternal uncles bowed to nephews and nephews’ sons. Chongtao asked to punish this by law.
translations.idiomatic: Between Tang and Liang, fleeing officials left the Ministry of Personnel’s files in tatters. Men turned the gap into profit—selling edicts, swapping senior and junior lines, even making uncles bow to nephews. Chongtao demanded legal punishment.

sentences.zh: 是時唐新滅梁，朝廷紀綱未立，議者以為宜革以漸，而崇韜疾惡太甚，果於必行，說、革心知其未可，而不能有所建言。

translations.literal: Tang had just destroyed Liang; court discipline was not yet established. Some argued reform should proceed gradually, but Chongtao hated corruption too fiercely and insisted on enforcement. Shuo and Ge knew this was premature but dared not object.
translations.idiomatic: Tang had just taken Liang; the court had no settled order. Some said reform should come step by step, but Chongtao’s hatred of abuse was too sharp and he would brook no delay. Shuo and Ge knew better but said nothing.

sentences.zh: 是歲冬，選人吳延皓改亡叔告身行事，事發，延皓及選吏尹玫皆坐死，尚書左丞判吏部銓崔沂等皆貶，說、革詣閣門待罪。

translations.literal: That winter a candidate, Wu Yanhao, falsified his deceased uncle’s appointment credentials. When the affair came to light, Yanhao and the examining clerk Yin Mei were both executed, and Vice Minister of Personnel Cui Yi and others were demoted. Shuo and Ge went to the palace gate to await punishment.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the candidate Wu Yanhao forged credentials for a dead uncle. Exposed, he and examiner Yin Mei were executed; Cui Yi and others in Personnel were demoted. Shuo and Ge waited at the gate to confess fault.

sentences.zh: 由是一以新法從事，往往以偽濫駁放而斃踣羈旅、號哭道路者，不可勝數。

translations.literal: From then on the new law was applied strictly. Many were rejected for forged or inflated credentials and left to die on the road, weeping in numbers beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the new rules were enforced to the letter. Countless men were turned away for fraud, stranded on the roads to die wailing.

sentences.zh: 及崇韜死，說乃教門人上書言其事，而議者亦以罪之。

translations.literal: After Chongtao died, Shuo had his student memorialize the affair, and critics blamed him for it.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongtao fell, Shuo had a protégé memorialize the matter—and was blamed for it.

sentences.zh: 是歲，大水，四方地連震，流民殍死者數萬人，軍士妻子皆采穭以食。

translations.literal: That year came great floods; earthquakes struck land after land; tens of thousands of refugees starved to death; soldiers’ wives and children gathered chaff to eat.
translations.idiomatic: That year floods and earthquakes ravaged the realm. Tens of thousands of wanderers starved; soldiers’ families ate chaff.

sentences.zh: 莊宗日以責三司使孔謙，謙不知所為。

translations.literal: Day by day Zhuangzong blamed Commissioner of the Three Departments Kong Qian, who had no answer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong daily blamed Kong Qian, commissioner of the Three Departments. Qian did not know what to do.

sentences.zh: 樞密小吏段徊曰：「臣嘗見前朝故事，國有大故，則天子以朱書御劄問宰相。

translations.literal: A young clerk in the Bureau of Military Affairs, Duan Hui, said: “I once saw precedent from the former dynasty—when the state faces great calamity, the emperor sends a red-ink imperial note to ask the chief councillors.
translations.idiomatic: A junior clerk in Military Affairs, Duan Hui, said: “I have seen old precedent—when the realm suffers great disaster, the emperor writes the chief councillors a personal note in red ink.

sentences.zh: 水旱，宰相職也。

translations.literal: Flood and drought are the chief councillors’ responsibility.”
translations.idiomatic: Flood and drought are the chief councillors’ business.”

sentences.zh: 」莊宗乃命學士草詔，手自書之，以問革、說。

translations.literal: ” Zhuangzong then had the academicians draft an edict, wrote it himself, and sent it to question Ge and Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhuangzong had the academicians draft an edict, copied it in his own hand, and sent it to Ge and Shuo.

sentences.zh: 革、說不能對，第曰：「陛下威德著於四海，今西兵破蜀，所得珍寶億萬，可以給軍。

translations.literal: Ge and Shuo could not answer. They only said: “Your Majesty’s prestige fills the four seas. The western army has broken Shu and obtained treasures beyond counting—we can supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: Ge and Shuo had no reply. They said only: “Your Majesty’s power is known everywhere. The western army has taken Shu and its treasure in the hundreds of millions—enough to pay the troops.

sentences.zh: 水旱，天之常道，不足憂也。

translations.literal: Flood and drought are heaven’s ordinary way—not worth worrying over.”
translations.idiomatic: Flood and drought are heaven’s way—nothing to fear.”

sentences.zh: 」革自為相，遭天下多故，而方服丹砂煉氣以求長生，嘗嘔血數日，幾死。

translations.literal: Since becoming chief councillor Ge had faced constant turmoil, yet he took cinnabar to refine his qi seeking longevity. He once vomited blood for days and nearly died.
translations.idiomatic: Ge had become chief councillor amid endless crisis, yet he swallowed cinnabar to cultivate breath and seek long life. Once he vomited blood for days and nearly died.

sentences.zh: 二人各以其子為拾遺，父子同省，人以為非，遽改佗官，而革以說子為弘文館學士，說以革子為集賢院學士。

translations.literal: Each man had made his son a remonstrator—they served in the same bureau, which people deemed improper. They quickly changed their sons to other posts, but Ge made Shuo’s son an academician of the Hongwen Hall and Shuo made Ge’s son an academician of the Jixian Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Each placed his son as a remonstrator; father and son in one office drew criticism. They hurriedly shifted the boys to other posts—Ge made Shuo’s son a Hongwen academician, Shuo made Ge’s son a Jixian academician.

sentences.zh: 莊宗崩，革為山陵使，莊宗已祔廟，革以故事當出鎮，乃還私第，數日未得命，而故人賓客趣使入朝。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong died, Ge was made overseer of the imperial tomb. After Zhuangzong was enshrined, by precedent Ge should have been sent to govern a circuit. He returned to his private residence. Days passed without a new appointment, until old friends and clients urged him to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong died; Ge was made tomb overseer. Once the late emperor was enshrined, custom called for Ge to take a provincial command. He went home and waited days for orders. Old associates pressed him to come to court.

sentences.zh: 樞密使安重誨詬之於朝曰：「山陵使名尚在，不俟改命，遽履新朝，以我武人可欺邪！

translations.literal: Chief Military Commissioner An Chonghui berated him in open court: “The title tomb overseer still stands—you did not wait for a new appointment but rushed into service under the new reign. Do you think us military men can be fooled!
translations.idiomatic: Chief Military Commissioner An Chonghui reviled him at court: “Your title as tomb overseer is still on the books—you did not wait for new orders but hurried into the new reign. Do you take us soldiers for fools!

sentences.zh: 」諫官希旨，上疏誣革縱田客殺人，說坐與鄰人爭井，遂俱罷。

translations.literal: ” Remonstrators seeking favor memorialized falsely that Ge let his tenant farmers kill someone, and Shuo was implicated for disputing a well with a neighbor. Both were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: ” Flattering remonstrators accused Ge of letting tenant farmers commit murder; Shuo was blamed for a quarrel over a well with a neighbor. Both lost office.

sentences.zh: 革貶辰州刺史，說漵州刺史，所在馳驛發遣。

translations.literal: Ge was demoted to prefect of Chen Prefecture and Shuo to prefect of Xu Prefecture; both were dispatched posthaste by relay.
translations.idiomatic: Ge was demoted to prefect of Chen and Shuo to prefect of Xu; relay horses hurried them on their way.

sentences.zh: 宰相鄭玨、任圜三上章，請毋行後命，不報。

translations.literal: Chief councillors Zheng Jue and Ren Huan submitted three memorials asking that the later orders not be carried out. No reply came.
translations.idiomatic: Chief councillors Zheng Jue and Ren Huan thrice memorialized to revoke the later punishments. The throne did not answer.

sentences.zh: 革復坐請俸私自入，說賣官與選人，責授革費州司戶參軍，說夷州司戶參軍，皆員外置同正員。

translations.literal: Ge was again punished for privately pocketing requested salary; Shuo for selling offices to candidates. Ge was reduced to registrar of Fei Prefecture and Shuo to registrar of Yi Prefecture—both supernumerary with regular rank.
translations.idiomatic: Ge was charged with keeping salary he had requested for himself; Shuo with selling posts to candidates. Ge became registrar of Fei and Shuo registrar of Yi—both supernumerary with full rank.

sentences.zh: 已而竄革陵州，說合州，皆長流百姓。

translations.literal: Soon Ge was exiled to Ling Prefecture and Shuo to He Prefecture—both long-term banishment among common people.
translations.idiomatic: Then Ge was banished to Ling and Shuo to He—long exile among the people.

sentences.zh: 初，說嘗以罪竄之南海，遇赦，還寓江陵，與高季興相知，及為相，常以書幣相問遺。

translations.literal: Earlier Shuo had been exiled to the South Seas for a crime, then pardoned and lodged at Jiangling, where he befriended Gao Jixing. As chief councillor he often exchanged letters and gifts with him.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo had once been banished to the South Seas, then pardoned and stayed at Jiangling, where he knew Gao Jixing. In office he kept up letters and gifts with him.

sentences.zh: 唐兵伐蜀，季興請以兵入三峽，莊宗許之，使季興自取夔、忠、萬、歸、峽等州為屬郡。

translations.literal: When Tang troops attacked Shu, Jixing asked to march through the Three Gorges. Zhuangzong agreed and let Jixing take Qian, Zhong, Wan, Gui, and Xia Prefectures as his own.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shu campaign Jixing asked to enter the Three Gorges with troops. Zhuangzong agreed and promised him Qian, Zhong, Wan, Gui, and Xia as subject prefectures.

sentences.zh: 及破蜀，季興無功，而唐用佗將取五州。

translations.literal: After Shu fell Jixing achieved nothing, while Tang used other generals to take the five prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Shu fell, but Jixing won nothing; Tang sent other generals to seize the five prefectures.

sentences.zh: 明宗初即位，季興數請五州，以謂先帝所許，朝廷不得已而與之。

translations.literal: When Mingzong first took the throne, Jixing repeatedly requested the five prefectures, citing the late emperor’s promise. The court had no choice but to grant them.
translations.idiomatic: At Mingzong’s accession Jixing demanded the five prefectures again, citing Zhuangzong’s pledge. The court yielded.

sentences.zh: 及革、說再貶，因以其事歸罪二人。

translations.literal: When Ge and Shuo were demoted again, the court blamed them for the affair.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge and Shuo were punished once more, the court pinned the matter on them.

sentences.zh: 天成二年夏，詔陵、合州刺史監賜自盡。

translations.literal: In summer of the second year of Tiancheng an edict had the prefects of Ling and He supervise their forced suicide.
translations.idiomatic: In summer of Tiancheng 2 an edict ordered the Ling and He prefects to oversee their suicides.

sentences.zh: 革子升，說子濤，皆官至尚書郎，坐其父廢。

translations.literal: Ge’s son Sheng and Shuo’s son Tao both reached Attendant Secretary rank before being disqualified because of their fathers.
translations.idiomatic: Ge’s son Sheng and Shuo’s son Tao had both risen to Attendant Secretary before their fathers’ fall ruined them.

sentences.zh: 至晉天福初，濤為尚書膳部員外郎，卒。

translations.literal: In early Tianfu of Jin, Tao was Attendant Secretary in the Board of Provisions and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jin’s Tianfu era Tao was Attendant Secretary of Provisions and died in post.

sentences.zh: ○盧程

translations.literal: Lu Cheng
translations.idiomatic: Lu Cheng

sentences.zh: 盧程，不知其世家何人也。

translations.literal: Lu Cheng—his family origins are unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Cheng’s lineage is unknown.

sentences.zh: 唐昭宗時，程舉進士，為鹽鐵出使巡官。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Zhaozong of Tang he passed the jinshi examination and served as inspection officer of the Salt and Iron Monopoly commission.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang Zhaozong he passed the jinshi and served as an inspection officer on the Salt and Iron commission.

sentences.zh: 唐亡，避亂燕、趙，變服為道士，遊諸侯間。

translations.literal: After Tang fell he fled the chaos to Yan and Zhao, changed clothes to become a Daoist priest, and wandered among regional lords.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang fell he fled to Yan and Zhao, dressed as a Daoist, and wandered among the warlords.

sentences.zh: 豆盧革為王處直判官，盧汝弼為河東節度副使，二人皆故唐時名族，與程門地相等，因共薦之以為河東節度推官。

translations.literal: Dou Luge was Wang Chuzhi’s aide, Lu Rubi was deputy military governor of Hedong—both were famous Tang clans equal in standing to Cheng’s family, so together they recommended him as investigating officer for Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Luge was Wang Chuzhi’s aide and Lu Rubi Hedong’s deputy governor—both old Tang great houses, Cheng’s equals in rank. Together they made him Hedong investigating officer.

sentences.zh: 莊宗嘗召程草文書，程辭不能。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong once summoned Cheng to draft documents. Cheng declined, saying he could not.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong once asked Cheng to draft documents. Cheng refused—he could not write them.

sentences.zh: 其後戰胡柳，掌書記王誠歿於陣，莊宗還軍太原，置酒謂監軍張承業曰：「吾以卮酒辟一書記於坐。

translations.literal: Later at the battle of Huliu chief secretary Wang Cheng died in combat. Zhuangzong returned to Taiyuan, set wine, and said to army supervisor Zhang Chengye: “I will use this cup of wine to appoint a secretary here at the table.
translations.idiomatic: At Huliu chief secretary Wang Cheng fell in battle. Zhuangzong returned to Taiyuan, poured wine, and told army supervisor Zhang Chengye: “With this cup I will appoint a secretary from those seated here.

sentences.zh: 」因舉卮屬巡官馮道。

translations.literal: ” He raised his cup and offered it to inspection officer Feng Dao.
translations.idiomatic: ” He lifted the cup and offered it to inspection officer Feng Dao.

sentences.zh: 程位在道上，以嘗辭不能，故不用，而遷程支使。

translations.literal: Cheng ranked above Dao, but because he had once declined saying he could not write, he was passed over; Cheng was made dispatch officer instead.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng outranked Dao, but having once refused to write, he was passed over. Cheng was made dispatch officer.

sentences.zh: 程大恨曰：「用人不以門閥而先田舍兒邪！」

translations.literal: Cheng hated this deeply and said: “They appoint men not by clan standing but give precedence to a country bumpkin!”
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was furious: “Men are chosen not by pedigree but for a farm boy!”

sentences.zh: 莊宗已即位，議擇宰相，而盧汝弼、蘇循已死，次節度判官盧質當拜，而質不樂行事，乃言豆盧革與程皆故唐時名族，可以為相，莊宗以程為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: After Zhuangzong took the throne they debated choosing chief councillors. Lu Rubi and Su Xun were dead; next in line was circuit aide Lu Zhi, who should have been appointed, but Zhi did not want the duties and said both Dou Luge and Cheng were famous Tang clans fit for chief councillor. Zhuangzong made Cheng Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Signatory Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong reigned they chose chief councillors. Lu Rubi and Su Xun were dead; Lu Zhi, the circuit aide, was next, but he did not want the post and said Dou Luge and Cheng, both old great houses, could serve. Zhuangzong made Cheng Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Signatory Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 是時，朝廷新造，百度未備，程、革拜命之日，肩輿導從，喧呼道中。

translations.literal: The court was newly established and institutions not yet complete. On the day Ge and Cheng took office, sedan chairs with attendants filled the roads shouting.
translations.idiomatic: The court was new and its rites unsettled. The day Ge and Cheng took office, sedan chairs and attendants clamored through the streets.

sentences.zh: 莊宗聞其聲以問左右，對曰：「宰相檐子入門。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong heard the noise and asked his attendants. They answered: “The chief councillors’ sedan chairs are entering the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong heard the uproar and asked what it was. They said: “The chief councillors’ litters are coming through the gate.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗登樓視之，笑曰：「所謂似是而非者也。」

translations.literal: ” Zhuangzong climbed a tower to watch and laughed: “So this is what they call ‘looks like it but isn’t.’”
translations.idiomatic: ” He climbed a tower to look and laughed: “So this is ‘seems so, but isn’t.’”

sentences.zh: 程奉皇太后冊，自魏至太原，上下山險，所至州縣，驅役丁夫，官吏迎拜，程坐肩輿自若，少忤其意，必加笞辱。

translations.literal: Cheng carried the empress dowager’s enfeoffment text from Wei to Taiyuan across dangerous mountains. At every prefecture and county he impressed laborers; officials bowed in welcome. Cheng sat in his sedan imperturbably and beat or humiliated anyone who slighted him.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng escorted the empress dowager’s patent from Wei to Taiyuan over steep passes. Every county he pressed corvée; officials bowed. He rode his litter at ease and whipped or abused any who crossed him.

sentences.zh: 人有假驢夫於程者，程帖興唐府給之，府吏啟無例，程怒笞吏背。

translations.literal: Someone asked Cheng to lend him a donkey handler. Cheng posted a note ordering Xingtang Prefecture to provide one. The prefectural clerk reported there was no precedent. Cheng angrily had the clerk beaten on the back.
translations.idiomatic: A man asked to borrow a donkey driver. Cheng posted an order on Xingtang Prefecture to supply one. The clerk said there was no precedent. Cheng had him flogged.

sentences.zh: 少尹任圜，莊宗姊婿也，詣程訴其不可。

translations.literal: Junior Prefect Ren Huan, Zhuangzong’s brother-in-law, came to Cheng to protest this was improper.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Prefect Ren Huan, Zhuangzong’s brother-in-law, went to Cheng to say this would not do.

sentences.zh: 程戴華陽巾，衣鶴氅，據幾決事，視圜罵曰：「爾何蟲豸，恃婦家力也！

translations.literal: Cheng wore a Huayang cap and crane-feather cloak, sat at his desk to decide affairs, looked at Huan and cursed: “What kind of insect are you, relying on your wife’s family’s power!
translations.idiomatic: Cheng wore a Huayang cap and crane cloak, sat at his desk, looked at Huan and snarled: “What vermin are you, leaning on your wife’s kin!

sentences.zh: 宰相取給州縣，何為不可！

translations.literal: Chief councillors take from prefectures and counties—what could be wrong with that!
translations.idiomatic: Chief councillors draw on prefectures and counties—why not!

sentences.zh: 」圜不對而去，夜馳至博州見莊宗。

translations.literal: ” Huan made no reply and left, then rode through the night to Bozhou to see Zhuangzong.
translations.idiomatic: ” Huan said nothing and left, then rode through the night to Bozhou to see Zhuangzong.

sentences.zh: 莊宗大怒，謂郭崇韜曰：「朕誤相此癡物，敢辱予九卿！

translations.literal: Zhuangzong was furious and said to Guo Chongtao: “I wrongly made chief councillor this fool—he dares insult my Nine Ministers!
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong raged and told Guo Chongtao: “I made this idiot chief councillor—and he insults my Nine Ministers!

sentences.zh: 」趣令自盡，崇韜亦欲殺之，賴盧質力解之，乃罷為右庶子。

translations.literal: ” He ordered Cheng to kill himself at once. Chongtao also wanted him executed, but Lu Zhi forcefully interceded, so Cheng was merely demoted to Right Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: ” He ordered Cheng to kill himself on the spot. Chongtao wanted him dead too, but Lu Zhi pleaded hard and Cheng was reduced to Right Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 莊宗入洛，程於路墜馬，中風卒，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Luoyang, Cheng fell from his horse on the road, had a stroke and died. He was posthumously made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: On the road to Luoyang Cheng fell from his horse, suffered a stroke, and died. He was posthumously made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 張文禮弒王镕，莊宗遣嗣昭討之。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenli murdered Wang Rong. Zhuangzong sent Sizhao to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenli killed Wang Rong. Zhuangzong sent Sizhao against him.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭戰歿，圜代將其軍，號令嚴肅。

translations.literal: Sizhao died in battle. Huan took command of his army with strict discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao fell in battle. Huan took his army and kept iron discipline.

sentences.zh: 既而文禮子處球等閉城堅守，不可下，圜數以禍福諭鎮人，鎮人信之。

translations.literal: Wenli’s son Chuchiu and others shut the city and held firm—it could not be taken. Huan repeatedly explained fortune and disaster to the townspeople, and they believed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenli’s son Chuchiu and others barred the city and would not yield. Huan again and again spoke of reward and ruin to the townsmen, and they trusted him.

sentences.zh: 圜嘗擁兵至城下，處球登城呼圜曰：「城中兵食俱盡，而久抗王師，若泥首自歸，懼無以塞責，幸公見哀，指其生路。

translations.literal: Huan once brought troops to the city walls. Chuchiu mounted the wall and called to Huan: “The city has exhausted its soldiers and food yet long resisted the imperial army. If we bow and surrender, we fear we cannot answer for our guilt. We beg your mercy—show us a way to live.
translations.idiomatic: Huan once marched to the walls. Chuchiu climbed the ramparts and called: “Soldiers and grain are gone, yet we long resisted the throne. If we bow in submission we may not atone. Show us mercy—point us a path to live.

sentences.zh: 」圜告之曰：「以子先人，固難容貸，然罰不及嗣，子可從輕。

translations.literal: ” Huan told him: “For your father’s crime you can hardly expect full pardon—but punishment does not extend to successors, so you may receive lighter sentence.
translations.idiomatic: ” Huan answered: “Your father’s crime is hard to forgive—but guilt does not pass to sons, so you may be treated lightly.

sentences.zh: 其如拒守經年，傷吾大將，一朝困竭，方布款誠，以此計之，子亦難免。

translations.literal: Yet you held out for years, killed our great general, and only now when exhausted do you show good faith—weighed this way, you too will be hard to spare.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you held out a year, killed our commander, and only now, spent, offer loyalty—weigh that, and you too may not escape.

sentences.zh: 然坐而待斃，曷若伏而俟命？

translations.literal: But to sit and await death—how is that better than bowing down and waiting for judgment?
translations.idiomatic: Still, to sit and die—is that better than bowing and awaiting judgment?

sentences.zh: 」處球流涕曰：「公言是也！

translations.literal: ” Chuchiu wept and said: “What you say is right!
translations.idiomatic: ” Chuchiu wept: “You speak truth!

sentences.zh: 」乃遣子送狀乞降，人皆稱圜其言不欺。

translations.literal: ” He sent his son with a surrender petition. Everyone praised Huan for speaking without deception.
translations.idiomatic: ” He sent his son with a surrender petition. All said Huan’s words were honest.

sentences.zh: 既而佗將攻破鎮州，處球雖見殺，而鎮之吏民以嘗乞降，故得保其家族者甚眾。

translations.literal: Later another general broke Zhenzhou. Chuchiu was killed, but many town officials and commoners who had surrendered were able to preserve their clans.
translations.idiomatic: Later another general took Zhenzhou. Chuchiu was killed, but many who had sought surrender kept their families.

sentences.zh: 其後以鎮州為北京，拜圜工部尚書，兼真定尹、北京副留守知留守事，為政有惠愛。

translations.literal: Later Zhenzhou was made Northern Capital. Huan was made Minister of Works, concurrent prefect of Zhending, deputy regent of the Northern Capital with regency authority—his governance was benevolent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzhou became the Northern Capital. Huan was made Minister of Works, prefect of Zhending, and deputy regent of the Northern Capital with full authority—his rule was kind.

sentences.zh: 明年，郭崇韜兼領成德軍節度使，改圜行軍司馬，仍知真定府事。

translations.literal: The next year Guo Chongtao also held Chengde circuit. Huan was changed to army march warden but retained Zhending prefecture duties.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Chongtao took Chengde as well. Huan became army march warden but still ran Zhending.

sentences.zh: 圜與崇韜素相善，又為其司馬，崇韜因以鎮州事托之，而圜多所違異。

translations.literal: Huan and Chongtao had always been on good terms, and Huan was his march warden, so Chongtao entrusted Zhenzhou affairs to him—but Huan often contradicted him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan and Chongtao had been close; as march warden Huan was entrusted with Zhenzhou—but he often crossed him.

sentences.zh: 初，圜推官張彭為人傾險貪黷，圜不能察，信任之，多為其所賣。

translations.literal: Huan’s investigating officer Zhang Peng was treacherous and corrupt. Huan failed to see this and trusted him, and Peng often betrayed him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan’s investigating officer Zhang Peng was scheming and greedy. Huan did not see it, trusted him, and was often betrayed.

sentences.zh: 及崇韜領鎮，彭為圜謀隱其公廨錢。

translations.literal: When Chongtao took the circuit, Peng advised Huan to conceal public office funds.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongtao governed the circuit, Peng urged Huan to hide public funds.

sentences.zh: 莊宗遣宦者選故趙王時宮人百餘，有許氏者尤有色，彭賂守者匿之。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong sent eunuchs to select over a hundred palace women from Former Zhao King’s time. One Xu was especially beautiful. Peng bribed the guards to hide her.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong sent eunuchs to choose more than a hundred palace women from the old Zhao court. One Lady Xu was especially fair. Peng bribed the keepers to conceal her.

sentences.zh: 後事覺，召彭詣京師，將罪之，彭懼，悉以前所隱公錢簿書獻崇韜，崇韜深德彭，不殺，由是與圜有隙。

translations.literal: When the affair came to light Peng was summoned to the capital for punishment. Terrified, he gave Chongtao all the ledgers of concealed public money. Chongtao was deeply grateful and spared him—creating a rift with Huan.
translations.idiomatic: When it was discovered Peng was called to the capital to be punished. In fear he handed Chongtao the ledgers of all he had hidden. Chongtao was grateful and spared him—and broke with Huan.

sentences.zh: 同光三年，圜罷司馬，守工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongguang Huan was removed as march warden and kept as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongguang 3 Huan lost the march warden post and remained Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 魏王繼岌暨崇韜伐蜀，懼圜攻己於後，乃辟圜參魏王軍事。

translations.literal: Prince of Wei Jiji and Chongtao campaigned against Shu. Fearing Huan would attack from behind, Jiji made Huan a military adviser to the Wei Prince’s army.
translations.idiomatic: Jiji and Chongtao marched on Shu. Jiji feared Huan might strike from the rear and made him staff officer on the Wei Prince’s campaign.

sentences.zh: 蜀滅，表圜黔南節度使，圜懇辭不就。

translations.literal: After Shu fell Jiji recommended Huan as military governor of Qiannan South. Huan earnestly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Shu fell; Jiji nominated Huan for Qiannan South. Huan refused firmly.

sentences.zh: 繼岌殺崇韜，以圜代將其軍而旋。

translations.literal: Jiji killed Chongtao and had Huan take command of his army and return.
translations.idiomatic: Jiji killed Chongtao and put Huan in command of the army for the march home.

sentences.zh: 康延孝反，繼岌遣圜將三千人，會董璋、孟知祥等兵，擊敗延孝於漢州，而魏王先至渭南，自殺，圜悉將其軍以東。

translations.literal: Kang Yanxiao rebelled. Jiji sent Huan with three thousand men to join Dong Zhang, Meng Zhixiang, and others, defeating Yanxiao at Han Prefecture. The Wei Prince reached Weinan first and killed himself. Huan led the entire army east.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Yanxiao rebelled. Jiji sent Huan with three thousand men to join Dong Zhang and Meng Zhixiang and crush Yanxiao at Han. The Wei Prince reached Weinan and killed himself. Huan brought the whole army east.

sentences.zh: 明宗嘉其功，拜圜同中書門下平章事，兼判三司。

translations.literal: Mingzong rewarded his merit and made Huan Co-Signatory Grand Councillor with concurrent charge of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong honored his service and made Huan Co-Signatory Grand Councillor, also running the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 是時，明宗新誅孔謙，圜選辟才俊，抑絕僥幸，公私給足，天下便之。

translations.literal: Mingzong had just executed Kong Qian. Huan selected talented men, suppressed favor-seekers—the public and private sectors were supplied and the realm benefited.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong had just killed Kong Qian. Huan recruited able men and shut out flatterers; public and private stores filled and the realm breathed easier.

sentences.zh: 是秋，韋說、豆盧革罷相，圜與安重誨、鄭玨、孔循議擇當為相者，圜意屬李琪，而玨、循雅不欲琪為相，謂重誨曰：「李琪非無文藝，但不廉耳！

translations.literal: That autumn Wei Shuo and Dou Luge were dismissed as chief councillors. Huan discussed with An Chonghui, Zheng Jue, and Kong Xun who should be chief councillor. Huan favored Li Qi, but Jue and Xun did not want Qi. They told Chonghui: “Li Qi has literary talent but lacks integrity!
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Wei Shuo and Dou Luge left office. Huan met with An Chonghui, Zheng Jue, and Kong Xun to choose a chief councillor. Huan wanted Li Qi; Jue and Xun did not. They told Chonghui: “Li Qi has talent but no honesty!

sentences.zh: 宰相，端方有器度者足以為之，太常卿崔協可也。

translations.literal: Chief councillor needs someone upright with bearing—Director of Ceremonies Cui Xie will do.”
translations.idiomatic: The post needs a man of dignity and measure—Director of Ceremonies Cui Xie will serve.”

sentences.zh: 」重誨以為然。

translations.literal: ” Chonghui agreed.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chonghui agreed.

sentences.zh: 佗日，明宗問誰可相者，重誨即以協對。

translations.literal: Another day Mingzong asked who could be chief councillor. Chonghui named Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Another day Mingzong asked whom to make chief councillor. Chonghui named Xie.

sentences.zh: 圜前爭曰：「重誨未諳朝廷人物，為人所賣。

translations.literal: Huan stepped forward and argued: “Chonghui does not know court personnel—he has been deceived.
translations.idiomatic: Huan spoke up: “Chonghui does not know the court—someone has sold him a lie.

sentences.zh: 天下皆知崔協不識文字，而虛有儀表，號為『沒字碑』。

translations.literal: Everyone knows Cui Xie cannot read yet has empty presence—they call him the ‘Stele Without Characters.’
translations.idiomatic: All the realm knows Cui Xie cannot read and is only a handsome shell—they call him the ‘Stele Without Characters.’

sentences.zh: 臣以陛下誤加采擢，無功幸進，此不知書，以臣一人取笑足矣，相位有幾，豈容更益笑端？

translations.literal: Your Majesty mistakenly promoted me without merit—one illiterate laughingstock is enough. How many chief councillor seats are there that we can add another source of ridicule?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty raised me without merit—one illiterate to mock is enough. How many chief councillor seats are there to add another joke?

sentences.zh: 」明宗曰：「宰相重位，卿等更自詳審。

translations.literal: ” Mingzong said: “Chief councillor is a weighty post—you must examine more carefully.
translations.idiomatic: ” Mingzong said: “Chief councillor is a heavy post—look again with care.

sentences.zh: 然吾在藩時，識易州刺史韋肅，世言肅名家子，且待我甚厚，置之此位可乎？

translations.literal: Yet when I was a prince I knew Prefect Wei Su of Yi Prefecture—a famous clan man who treated me well. Could he hold this post?
translations.idiomatic: When I was in the provinces I knew Wei Su, prefect of Yi—a man of a great house who treated me well. Could he serve?

sentences.zh: 肅或未可，則馮書記先朝判官，稱為長者，可以相矣！

translations.literal: If Su will not do, then Secretary Feng—the former Tang aide called a man of worth—could serve as chief councillor!
translations.idiomatic: If Su will not do, then Secretary Feng—the old Tang aide, called a man of worth—could be chief councillor!

sentences.zh: 」馮書記者，道也。

translations.literal: ” Secretary Feng was Dao.
translations.idiomatic: ” Secretary Feng was Feng Dao.

sentences.zh: 議未決，重誨等退休於中興殿廓下，孔循不揖，拂衣而去，行且罵曰：「天下事一則任圜，二則任圜，圜乃何人！

translations.literal: Before a decision was reached Chonghui and the others withdrew to the corridor of the Zhongxing Hall. Kong Xun did not bow, brushed his robes and left, cursing as he went: “State affairs—first Ren Huan, second Ren Huan! Who is Ren Huan!
translations.idiomatic: Before they decided, Chonghui and the rest retired to the Zhongxing Hall corridor. Kong Xun did not bow, shook out his sleeves and left, cursing: “The realm—first Ren Huan, second Ren Huan! Who is Ren Huan!

sentences.zh: 」圜謂重誨曰：「李琪才藝，可兼時輩百人，而讒夫巧沮，忌害其能，若舍琪而相協，如棄蘇合之丸而取蜣蜋之轉也！

translations.literal: ” Huan told Chonghui: “Li Qi’s talent surpasses a hundred men of this age, yet slanderers obstruct him out of envy. If we abandon Qi and make Xie chief councillor, it is like discarding musk pills for dung beetle balls!
translations.idiomatic: ” Huan told Chonghui: “Li Qi’s gifts outmatch a hundred of our peers, yet slanderers block him from envy. To drop Qi for Xie is to throw away musk for dung-beetle balls!

sentences.zh: 」重誨笑而止。

translations.literal: ” Chonghui laughed and said no more.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chonghui laughed and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 然重誨終以循言為信，居月余，協與馮道皆拜相。

translations.literal: Yet in the end Chonghui took Xun’s word as trustworthy; after more than a month, both Xie and Feng Dao were appointed chief councillors.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Chonghui trusted Kong Xun in the end. A month later, Cui Xie and Feng Dao both became chief councillors.

sentences.zh: 協在相位數年，人多嗤其所為，然圜與重誨交惡自協始。

translations.literal: Xie held the chief councillor’s post for several years. Many mocked what he did. Yet Yuan’s falling out with Chonghui began with Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Xie sat as chief councillor for years while men laughed at his deeds. Yuan’s breach with Chonghui began there.

sentences.zh: 故事，使臣出四方，皆自戶部給券，重誨奏請自內出，圜以故事爭之，不能得，遂與重誨辨於帝前，圜聲色俱厲。

translations.literal: By precedent, envoys sent abroad all received travel vouchers from the Ministry of Revenue. Chonghui memorialized asking that they be issued from within the palace instead. Yuan contested this citing precedent but could not prevail, and argued with Chonghui before the emperor—Yuan’s voice and bearing both fierce.
translations.idiomatic: By old rule, envoys abroad drew travel vouchers from the Ministry of Revenue. Chonghui asked that they come from the palace instead. Yuan fought him on precedent and lost, then quarreled with Chonghui before the throne—voice and face both hard.

sentences.zh: 明宗罷朝，後宮嬪御迎前問曰：「與重誨論者誰？

translations.literal: When Mingzong dismissed court, the palace consorts came forward and asked: "Who was arguing with Chonghui?
translations.idiomatic: Court ended. Palace consorts met Mingzong and asked: "Who was arguing with Chonghui?

sentences.zh: 」明宗曰：「宰相也。

translations.literal: " Mingzong said: "The chief councillor."
translations.idiomatic: " Mingzong said: "The chief councillor."

sentences.zh: 」宮人奏曰：「妾在長安，見宰相奏事，未嘗如此，蓋輕大家耳！

translations.literal: " The palace woman said: "When I was in Chang’an, I saw chief councillors report affairs—I never saw it like this. They must look down on Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: " A palace woman said: "In Chang’an I watched chief councillors report to the throne—I never saw such a scene. They must hold Your Majesty cheap!

sentences.zh: 」明宗由是不悅，而使臣給券卒自內出，圜益憤沮。

translations.literal: " From this Mingzong was displeased, and envoys’ vouchers in the end were issued from within the palace. Yuan grew all the more angry and dejected.
translations.idiomatic: " Mingzong took offense. Envoys’ vouchers were issued from the palace after all, and Yuan sank deeper into rage and despair.

sentences.zh: 重誨嘗過圜，圜出妓，善歌而有色，重誨欲之，圜不與，由是二人益相惡。

translations.literal: Once when Chonghui visited Yuan, Yuan brought out a singing-girl—skilled in song and beautiful. Chonghui wanted her; Yuan would not give her up. From this the two hated each other all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui once called on Yuan, who produced a courtesan—fair and fine of voice. Chonghui wanted her; Yuan refused. Their hatred deepened.

sentences.zh: 而圜遽求罷職，乃罷為太子少保。

translations.literal: Yuan then urgently requested to leave office and was demoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan begged to leave office at once and was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 圜不自安，因請致仕，退居於磁州。

translations.literal: Yuan felt unsafe, asked to retire, and withdrew to live in Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy in his post, Yuan asked to retire and went home to Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 朱守殷反於汴州，重誨誣圜與守殷連謀，遣人矯制殺之。

translations.literal: Zhu Shouyin rebelled at Bianzhou. Chonghui falsely accused Yuan of plotting with Shouyin and sent men with a forged edict to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shouyin rose at Bianzhou. Chonghui charged Yuan with plotting alongside him and sent killers bearing a forged edict.

sentences.zh: 圜受命怡然，聚族酣飲而死。

translations.literal: Yuan received the order calmly, gathered his clan for a feast, and died drunk.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan took the order calmly, gathered his kin for a last feast, and died in his cups.

sentences.zh: 明宗知而不問，為下詔，坐圜與守殷通書而言涉怨望。

translations.literal: Mingzong knew but did not inquire. He issued an edict charging Yuan with exchanging letters with Shouyin in language of resentment and discontent.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong knew and said nothing. An edict charged Yuan with writing Shouyin in tones of grievance and disaffection.

sentences.zh: 湣帝即位，贈圜太傅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min took the throne, Yuan was posthumously made Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min succeeded, Yuan was posthumously made Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 莊宗及劉皇后幸河南尹張全義第，酒酣，命皇后拜全義為父。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong and Empress Liu visited the residence of Henan governor Zhang Quanyi. When the wine was deep, Zhuangzong ordered the empress to bow and acknowledge Quanyi as father.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong and Empress Liu visited Henan governor Zhang Quanyi at home. Deep in wine, Zhuangzong had the empress bow and call Quanyi father.

sentences.zh: 明日，遣宦者命學士作箋上全義，以父事之，鳳上書極言其不可。

translations.literal: The next day he sent a eunuch to order an academician to draft a memorial to Quanyi treating him as a father. Feng submitted a memorial strongly arguing this was impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Next day a eunuch ordered an academician to draft a memorial honoring Quanyi as a father. Feng memorialized that it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 全義養子郝繼孫犯法死，宦官、伶人冀其貲財，固請籍沒，鳳又上書言：「繼孫為全義養子，不宜有別籍之財，而於法不至籍沒，刑人利財，不可以示天下。

translations.literal: Quanyi’s adopted son Hao Jisun died for a crime. Eunuchs and actors hoped for his property and firmly petitioned for confiscation. Feng again submitted a memorial saying: "Jisun was Quanyi’s adopted son. He should not have property under a separate household register, and by law confiscation does not reach so far. Profiting from a convict’s wealth cannot be shown to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi’s adopted son Hao Jisun died for a crime. Eunuchs and actors eyed his estate and pressed for confiscation. Feng wrote again: "Jisun was Quanyi’s adopted son. He ought not to hold wealth under a separate register, and the law does not call for seizure. To profit from a condemned man’s goods is no lesson for the realm.

sentences.zh: 」是時，皇后及群小用事，鳳言皆不見納。

translations.literal: " At that time the empress and petty men held power; none of Feng’s words was heeded.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress and her petty favorites ruled; none of Feng’s words was heard.

sentences.zh: 明宗武君，不通文字，四方章奏，常使安重誨讀之。

translations.literal: Mingzong was a military man who did not know writing. Memorials from the four directions were usually read to him by An Chonghui.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong was a soldier who could not read. Memorials from every quarter were usually read aloud by An Chonghui.

sentences.zh: 重誨亦不知書，奏讀多不稱旨。

translations.literal: Chonghui too could not read. His readings of memorials often missed the emperor’s intent.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui could not read either. His readings often missed the mark.

sentences.zh: 孔循教重誨求儒者置之左右，而兩人皆不知唐故事，於是置端明殿學士，以馮道及鳳為之。

translations.literal: Kong Xun taught Chonghui to seek Confucian scholars and place them at hand. But neither knew Tang precedent, so they established Duanming Hall academicians, with Feng Dao and Feng as holders.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Xun urged Chonghui to keep Confucian scholars close. Neither man knew Tang precedent, so they created Duanming Hall academicians and named Feng Dao and Zhao Feng to the posts.

sentences.zh: 鳳好直言而性剛強，素與任圜善，自圜為相，頗薦進之。

translations.literal: Feng was fond of straight speech and of a stubborn nature. He had always been on good terms with Ren Yuan; once Yuan became chief councillor, he recommended Feng for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Feng loved blunt truth and had a hard nature. He and Ren Yuan had long been friends; once Yuan became chief councillor, he pushed Feng forward.

sentences.zh: 初，端明殿學士班在翰林學士下，而結銜又在官下。

translations.literal: At first, Duanming Hall academicians ranked below Hanlin academicians, and their formal title lines were also below their office rank.
translations.idiomatic: At first Duanming Hall academicians ranked below the Hanlin, and even their title lines sat beneath their offices.

sentences.zh: 明年，鳳遷禮部侍郎，因諷圜升學士於官上，又詔班在翰林學士上。

translations.literal: The next year Feng was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites. He therefore hinted to Yuan to raise the academicians’ title above their office rank. An edict also placed their rank above Hanlin academicians.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Feng became Vice Minister of Rites and nudged Yuan to lift the academicians’ titles above their offices. An edict also set them above the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 圜為重誨所殺，而誣以謀反。

translations.literal: Yuan was killed by Chonghui and falsely charged with plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui killed Yuan and smeared him with a charge of treason.

sentences.zh: 是時，重誨方用事，雖明宗不能詰也，鳳獨號哭呼重誨曰：「任圜天下義士，豈肯謀反！

translations.literal: At that time Chonghui was in power; even Mingzong could not question him. Feng alone wailed and cried out to Chonghui: "Ren Yuan is an upright man of the realm—how would he rebel!
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui then held the reins; even Mingzong could not press him. Feng alone wept and shouted at Chonghui: "Ren Yuan is a man of honor under heaven—would he rebel!

sentences.zh: 而公殺之，何以示天下？

translations.literal: Yet you killed him—how do you show that to the realm?
translations.idiomatic: You killed him—what do you show the realm?

sentences.zh: 」重誨慚不能對。

translations.literal: " Chonghui was ashamed and could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: " Chonghui flushed and had no reply.

sentences.zh: 術士周玄豹以相法言人事多中，莊宗尤信重之，以為北京巡官。

translations.literal: The diviner Zhou Xuanbao, using physiognomy, often hit the mark on human affairs. Zhuangzong especially trusted and valued him, making him northern-capital touring officer.
translations.idiomatic: The physiognomist Zhou Xuanbao often read men correctly. Zhuangzong trusted him deeply and made him touring officer of the northern capital.

sentences.zh: 明宗為內衙指揮使，重誨欲試玄豹，乃使佗人與明宗易服，而坐明宗於下坐，召玄豹相之，玄豹曰：「內衙，貴將也，此不足當之。

translations.literal: When Mingzong was commander of the inner guard, Chonghui wished to test Xuanbao. He had someone swap clothes with Mingzong and seated Mingzong in a lower seat, then summoned Xuanbao to read his face. Xuanbao said: "The inner guard—an eminent general—this man is not equal to it.
translations.idiomatic: While Mingzong commanded the inner guard, Chonghui tested Xuanbao. He had another man swap clothes with Mingzong and set Mingzong in a low seat, then called Xuanbao in. Xuanbao said: "The inner guard is a great commander’s post—this man cannot fill it.

sentences.zh: 」乃指明宗於下坐曰：「此是也！

translations.literal: " He then pointed to Mingzong in the lower seat: "This is the one!
translations.idiomatic: " He pointed to Mingzong below: "This is the man!

sentences.zh: 」因為明宗言其後貴不可言。

translations.literal: " He then told Mingzong his future honor was beyond words.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he told Mingzong his rise would be beyond telling.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，思玄豹以為神，將召至京師，鳳諫曰：「好惡，上所慎也。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, he thought Xuanbao divine and was about to summon him to the capital. Feng remonstrated: "Likes and dislikes—what the sovereign must be careful of.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong took the throne, thought Xuanbao miraculous, and meant to summon him to court. Feng warned: "Likes and dislikes are what a ruler must guard.

sentences.zh: 今陛下神其術而召之，則傾國之人，皆將奔走吉兇之說，轉相惑亂，為患不細。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty treats his art as miraculous and summons him, then everyone in the realm will rush after fortune and disaster lore, passing confusion from one to another—the harm is no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty treats his craft as sacred and calls him in, the whole realm will run after omens of luck and ruin, trading lies until the court is poisoned—the harm is not small.

sentences.zh: 」明宗遂不復召。

translations.literal: " Mingzong then did not summon him again.
translations.idiomatic: " Mingzong never summoned him again.

sentences.zh: 朱守殷反，明宗幸汴州，守殷已誅，又詔幸鄴。

translations.literal: Zhu Shouyin rebelled. Mingzong went to Bianzhou. Shouyin was already executed, yet an edict also ordered a visit to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shouyin rebelled. Mingzong went to Bian; Shouyin was already dead, yet an edict still ordered a visit to Ye.

sentences.zh: 是時，從駕諸軍方自河南徙家至汴，不欲北行，軍中為之洶洶。

translations.literal: At that time the armies accompanying the emperor had just moved their families from Henan to Bian and did not wish to go north; the army was agitated.
translations.idiomatic: The armies with the throne had just moved their families from Henan to Bian and did not want to march north. The camps seethed.

sentences.zh: 而定州王都以為天子幸汴州誅守殷，又幸鄴以圖己，因疑不自安。

translations.literal: Wang Du of Dingzhou thought the Son of Heaven had come to Bian to execute Shouyin and now visited Ye to target him; he grew suspicious and uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Du of Dingzhou thought the emperor had come to Bian to kill Shouyin and now meant to visit Ye against him. He turned fearful and restless.

sentences.zh: 宰相率百官詣閣，請罷幸鄴，明宗不聽，人情大恐，群臣不復敢言。

translations.literal: The chief councillor led the hundred officials to the gate and asked that the Ye visit be cancelled. Mingzong would not listen. Public sentiment was greatly fearful; the ministers no longer dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: The chief councillor led the hundred officials to the gate and begged that the Ye visit be dropped. Mingzong would not hear it. Fear spread through the court; no one else dared speak.

sentences.zh: 鳳手疏責安重誨，言甚切直，重誨以白，遂罷幸。

translations.literal: Feng submitted a personal memorial rebuking An Chonghui in very sharp, direct language. Chonghui reported it to the emperor, and the Ye visit was cancelled.
translations.idiomatic: Feng wrote a private memorial scolding An Chonghui in the sharpest terms. Chonghui passed it to the throne, and the Ye visit was cancelled.

sentences.zh: 有僧遊西域，得佛牙以獻，明宗以示大臣。

translations.literal: A monk who had traveled the Western Regions obtained a Buddha’s tooth and presented it. Mingzong showed it to the great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: A monk back from the Western Regions brought a Buddha’s tooth as tribute. Mingzong showed it to his ministers.

sentences.zh: 鳳言：「世傳佛牙水火不能傷，請驗其真偽。

translations.literal: Feng said: "Tradition holds that a Buddha’s tooth cannot be harmed by fire or water. Please test whether it is genuine.
translations.idiomatic: Feng said: "They say a Buddha’s tooth cannot be touched by fire or water. Let us test it.

sentences.zh: 」因以斧斫之，應手而碎。

translations.literal: " He then struck it with an axe; it shattered at once.
translations.idiomatic: " He took an axe to it; it broke at a blow.

sentences.zh: 是時，宮中施物已及數千，因鳳碎之乃止。

translations.literal: At that time palace donations of relics had already reached several thousand; because Feng smashed this one, they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Palace relic offerings had already passed several thousand; after Feng shattered this one, the gifts stopped.

sentences.zh: 天成四年夏，拜門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In summer of the fourth year of Tiancheng, he was appointed Vice Director of the Chancellery and Co-Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Tiancheng’s fourth year he became Vice Director of the Chancellery and Co-Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 秘書少監於嶠者，自莊宗時與鳳俱為翰林學士，而嶠亦訐直敢言，與鳳素善。

translations.literal: Yu Qiao, Vice Director of the Secretariat, had served with Feng as Hanlin academician since Zhuangzong’s time. Qiao too was blunt and daring to speak, and he and Feng had long been on good terms.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qiao, Vice Director of the Secretariat, had been Hanlin academician with Feng since Zhuangzong’s day. Qiao was blunt and fearless too, and the two were old friends.

sentences.zh: 及鳳已貴，而嶠久不遷，自以材名在鳳上而不用，因與蕭希甫數非斥時政，尤詆訾鳳，鳳心銜之，未有以發。

translations.literal: Once Feng had risen high while Qiao long went without promotion, Qiao felt his talent and name outranked Feng’s yet he was unused. He therefore joined Xiao Xifu in repeatedly denouncing current policy, especially reviling Feng. Feng nursed resentment but had no opening to act.
translations.idiomatic: Feng rose while Qiao stalled. Qiao thought himself the better man by talent and name, yet sat idle. He and Xiao Xifu began to rail at the times and especially at Feng. Feng brooded but had no opening.

sentences.zh: 而嶠與鄰家爭水竇，為安重誨所怒，鳳即左遷嶠秘書少監。

translations.literal: Then Qiao quarreled with a neighbor over a water channel and incurred An Chonghui’s anger. Feng immediately demoted Qiao to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao quarreled with a neighbor over a water sluice and angered An Chonghui. Feng at once demoted him to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 嶠因被酒往見鳳，鳳知其必不遜，乃辭以沐發，嶠詬直吏，又溺於從者直盧而去。

translations.literal: Qiao, drunk, went to see Feng. Feng knew he would surely be insolent and pleaded that he was washing his hair. Qiao cursed the clerks on duty and urinated in the attendants’ quarters before leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, Qiao went to Feng’s door. Feng knew he would be rude and begged off, saying he was washing his hair. Qiao cursed the clerks and pissed in the attendants’ hall on his way out.

sentences.zh: 省吏白鳳，嶠溺於客次，且詬鳳。

translations.literal: The office clerks reported to Feng that Qiao had urinated in the guest reception area and also cursed Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Office clerks told Feng that Qiao had urinated in the guest hall and cursed him by name.

sentences.zh: 鳳以其事聞，明宗下詔奪嶠官，長流武州百姓，又流振武，天下冤之。

translations.literal: Feng reported the affair to the throne. Mingzong issued an edict stripping Qiao of office, exiling him as a commoner of Wuzhou, then further to Zhenwu. All under heaven thought it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Feng reported it. Mingzong stripped Qiao of rank, exiled him as a commoner of Wuzhou, then sent him farther to Zhenwu. The realm cried injustice.

sentences.zh: 其後安重誨為邊彥溫等告變，明宗詔彥溫等廷詰，具伏其詐，即斬之。

translations.literal: Later An Chonghui was reported for plotting by Bian Yanwen and others. Mingzong ordered Yanwen and the rest examined in court; they fully confessed their fraud and were immediately beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Later Bian Yanwen and others denounced An Chonghui for treason. Mingzong had them questioned in open court; they confessed the frame-up and were beheaded at once.

sentences.zh: 後數日，鳳奏事中興殿，啟曰：「臣聞奸人有誣重誨者。

translations.literal: Some days later Feng was reporting affairs in the Zhongxing Hall and opened by saying: "Your servant has heard that villains falsely accused Chonghui.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Feng was reporting business in the Zhongxing Hall and began: "I have heard that knaves falsely accused Chonghui.

sentences.zh: 」明宗曰：「此閑事，朕已處置之，卿可無問也。

translations.literal: " Mingzong said: "This is a trivial matter. I have already handled it—you need not ask.
translations.idiomatic: " Mingzong said: "That is a small matter. I have already settled it—you need not inquire.

sentences.zh: 」鳳曰：「臣所聞者，系國家利害，陛下不可以為閑。

translations.literal: " Feng said: "What Your servant heard concerns the state’s profit and harm. Your Majesty cannot treat it as trivial.
translations.idiomatic: " Feng said: "What I heard touches the state’s weal and woe. Your Majesty cannot call it small.

sentences.zh: 」因指殿屋曰：「此殿所以尊嚴宏壯者，棟樑柱石之所扶持也，若折其一棟，去其一柱，則傾危矣。

translations.literal: " Pointing at the hall he said: "This hall stands solemn and grand because beams, pillars, and foundation stones uphold it. Break one beam, remove one pillar, and it will topple.
translations.idiomatic: " He pointed at the hall: "This hall stands tall because beams, pillars, and stones hold it up. Break one beam, pull one pillar, and it falls.

sentences.zh: 大臣，國之棟樑柱石也，且重誨起微賤，歷艱危，致陛下為中興主，安可使奸人動搖！

translations.literal: Great ministers are the beams, pillars, and foundation stones of the state. Moreover, Chonghui rose from humble station, passed through peril, and helped Your Majesty become the Restorer—how can villains be allowed to shake him!
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers are the state’s beams and pillars. Chonghui rose from nothing, passed through danger, and helped Your Majesty become the Restorer—how can knaves be allowed to shake him!

sentences.zh: 」明宗改容謝之曰：「卿言是也。

translations.literal: " Mingzong changed expression and apologized: "You speak rightly."
translations.idiomatic: " Mingzong’s face changed and he apologized: "You are right."

sentences.zh: 」遂族彥溫等三家。

translations.literal: " The clans of Yanwen and the others were then exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: " The clans of Yanwen and his fellows were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 其後重誨得罪，群臣無敢言者，獨鳳數言重誨盡忠。

translations.literal: Later, when Chonghui fell from favor, none of the great ministers dared speak for him; only Feng repeatedly said Chonghui had been utterly loyal.
translations.idiomatic: When Chonghui later fell, no minister dared speak for him—only Feng, again and again, said he had been utterly loyal.

sentences.zh: 明宗以鳳為朋黨，罷為安國軍節度使。

translations.literal: Mingzong took Feng for a faction-man and dismissed him to serve as military governor of the Anguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong marked Feng as a partisan and sent him out as military governor of the Anguo Army.

sentences.zh: 鳳在鎮所得俸祿，悉以分將校賓客。

translations.literal: The salary Feng received in his command he gave entirely to his officers and guests.
translations.idiomatic: In the provinces Feng divided his entire salary among officers and guests.

sentences.zh: 廢帝入立，召為太子太保。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, Feng was recalled as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor succeeded, Feng was recalled as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 病足居於家，疾篤，自筮，投蓍而嘆曰：「吾家世無五十者，又皆窮賤，吾今壽過其數而富貴，復何求哉！

translations.literal: His feet afflicted, he stayed home. When his illness grew grave he divined for himself, cast the yarrow stalks, and sighed: "No one in my family has ever lived to fifty; all have been poor and lowly. I have now passed that number in years and live in wealth and honor—what more could I seek!
translations.idiomatic: His feet failed him and he kept to his house. Near death he divined for himself, cast the stalks, and sighed: "No one in my line has ever seen fifty; all died poor and obscure. I have outlived that count and tasted wealth—what more is there to want!

sentences.zh: 」清泰二年卒於家。

translations.literal: " He died at home in the second year of Qingtai.
translations.idiomatic: " He died at home in Qingtai’s second year.

sentences.zh: 李襲吉

translations.literal: Li Xiji
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiji

sentences.zh: 李襲吉，父圖，洛陽人，或曰唐相林甫之後也。

translations.literal: Li Xiji’s father Tu was a man of Luoyang; some say he was descended from the Tang chief councillor Lin Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiji’s father Tu came from Luoyang; some say he descended from the Tang chief councillor Lin Fu.

sentences.zh: 乾符中，襲吉舉進士，為河中節度使李都搉鹽判官。

translations.literal: In the Qianfu era Xiji passed the jinshi examination and served as salt-assessment aide to Hedong military governor Li Du.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianfu era Xiji passed the jinshi and became salt-assessment aide to Hedong governor Li Du.

sentences.zh: 後去之晉，晉王以為榆次令，遂為掌書記。

translations.literal: Later he left for Jin. The Prince of Jin made him magistrate of Yuci, and he then became chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He later went to Jin. The Prince of Jin made him magistrate of Yuci, then chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 襲吉博學，多知唐故事。

translations.literal: Xiji was broadly learned and knew much of Tang precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Xiji was widely read and knew Tang precedent well.

sentences.zh: 遷節度副使，官至諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to deputy military governor and reached the office of Remonstrating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to deputy military governor and reached Remonstrating Censor.

sentences.zh: 晉王與梁有隙，交兵累年，後晉王數困，欲與梁通和，使襲吉為書諭梁，辭甚辨麗。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin and Liang were at odds and fought for years. Later the Prince of Jin was repeatedly hard pressed and wished to make peace with Liang. He had Xiji draft a letter instructing Liang—its language very eloquent and polished.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin and Liang feuded and fought for years. When Jin grew hard pressed, the prince sought peace and had Xiji draft the letter to Liang—eloquent and sharp.

sentences.zh: 梁太祖使人讀之，至於「毒手尊拳，交相於暮夜，金戈鐵馬，蹂踐於明時」，嘆曰：「李公僻處一隅，有士如此，使吾得之，傅虎以翼也！

translations.literal: The Liang Founding Emperor had someone read it. When it reached the lines "Poisoned hands and clenched fists meet in the dark of night; golden spears and iron horses trample the bright age," he sighed: "Master Li sits in a corner with men like this—had I gained him, it would be like fitting wings to a tiger!
translations.idiomatic: The Liang Founding Emperor had it read aloud. At "Poisoned hands and iron fists in the midnight dark; golden spears and iron horses trampling the bright age," he sighed: "Master Li holds one corner of the realm yet keeps men like this—had I won him, it would be wings on a tiger!

sentences.zh: 」顧其從事敬翔曰：「善為我答之。

translations.literal: " He turned to his aide Jing Xiang: "Write me a worthy reply.
translations.idiomatic: " He told his aide Jing Xiang: "Answer him well for me.

sentences.zh: 」及翔所答，書辭不工，而襲吉之書，多傳於世。

translations.literal: " When Xiang’s reply came, its language was poor, while Xiji’s letter was widely copied in the world.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiang’s answer was clumsy, but Xiji’s letter passed hand to hand across the realm.

sentences.zh: 襲吉為人恬淡，以文辭自娛，天祐三年卒。

translations.literal: Xiji was by nature calm and took pleasure in literary craft. He died in the third year of Tianyou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiji was calm by nature and amused himself with letters. He died in Tianyou’s third year.

sentences.zh: 以盧汝弼代為副使。

translations.literal: Lu Rubi replaced him as deputy governor.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Rubi replaced him as deputy governor.

sentences.zh: 莊宗即位，贈襲吉禮部尚書、汝弼兵部尚書。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne, Xiji was posthumously made Minister of Rites and Rubi Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhuangzong’s accession Xiji was posthumously made Minister of Rites and Rubi Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 莊宗幸東都，定州王都來朝，莊宗命憲治鞠場，與都擊鞠。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong visited the eastern capital. Wang Du of Dingzhou came to court. Zhuangzong ordered Xian to prepare the cuju ground and play cuju with Du.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong visited the eastern capital. Wang Du of Dingzhou came to court. Zhuangzong had Xian ready the cuju ground and play with Du.

sentences.zh: 初，莊宗建號於東都，以鞠場為即位壇，於是憲言：「即位壇，王者所以興也。

translations.literal: At first, when Zhuangzong established his title at the eastern capital, he had used the cuju ground as the enthronement altar. Xian therefore said: "The enthronement altar is what a true king uses to rise.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong first took the title at the eastern capital, the cuju ground had been his enthronement altar. Xian said: "An enthronement altar is where a king rises.

sentences.zh: 漢高阝南、魏繁陽壇，至今皆在，不可毀。

translations.literal: Han Gaozu’s altar at Zannan and Wei’s altar at Fanyang stand to this day—they must not be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gaozu’s altar at Zannan and Wei’s altar at Fanyang still stand—they must not be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 」乃別治宮西為鞠場，場未成，莊宗怒，命兩虞候亟毀壇以為場。

translations.literal: " A separate site west of the palace was prepared as the cuju ground. Before it was finished Zhuangzong raged and ordered the two camp commanders to destroy the altar at once and make it the ground.
translations.idiomatic: " They built a new ground west of the palace. Before it was done Zhuangzong raged and ordered both camp commanders to tear down the altar and make the field.

sentences.zh: 憲退而嘆曰：「此不祥之兆也！」

translations.literal: Xian withdrew and sighed: "This is an ill omen!"
translations.idiomatic: Xian withdrew and sighed: "This is an ill omen!"

sentences.zh: 初，明宗北伐契丹，取魏鎧仗以給軍，有細鎧五百，憲遂給之而不以聞。

translations.literal: At first, when Mingzong marched north against the Khitan, he took Wei’s armor and weapons to supply the army. There were five hundred sets of fine armor; Xian issued them without reporting it.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong marched north against the Khitan, he drew on Wei’s stores to arm the host. Five hundred sets of fine armor passed through Xian’s hands without report.

sentences.zh: 莊宗至魏，大怒，責憲馳自取之，左右諫之乃止。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong reached Wei he was furious and ordered Xian to ride and fetch them himself. Those around him remonstrated and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong reached Wei in a fury and ordered Xian to ride and fetch the armor himself. Attendants talked him down.

sentences.zh: 又問憲庫錢幾何。

translations.literal: He also asked Xian how much money was in the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked how much cash the treasury held.

sentences.zh: 憲上庫簿有錢三萬緡，莊宗益怒，謂其嬖伶史彥瓊曰：「我與群臣飲博，須錢十餘萬，而憲以故紙給我。

translations.literal: Xian submitted the ledger showing thirty thousand strings of cash. Zhuangzong grew angrier still and said to his favorite actor Shi Yanqiong: "When I drink and gamble with my ministers, I need more than a hundred thousand strings of cash, and Xian gives me old ledger paper.
translations.idiomatic: Xian showed the books: thirty thousand strings. Zhuangzong burned hotter and told his favorite actor Shi Yanqiong: "When I drink and gamble with my ministers I need more than a hundred thousand strings, and Xian feeds me dead ledgers.

sentences.zh: 我未渡河時，庫錢常百萬緡，今復何在？

translations.literal: Before I crossed the river, the treasury held a million strings—where has it gone now?
translations.idiomatic: Before I crossed the river the vault held a million strings—where did it go?

sentences.zh: 」彥瓊為憲解之乃已。

translations.literal: " Yanqiong explained on Xian’s behalf and the matter ended.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanqiong pleaded for Xian and the storm passed.

sentences.zh: 郭崇韜伐蜀，薦憲可任為相，而宦官、伶人不欲憲在朝廷，樞密承旨段徊曰：「宰相在天子面前，事有非是，尚可改作，一方之任，茍非其人，則為患不細。

translations.literal: Guo Chongtao’s campaign against Shu recommended Xian as fit to serve as chief councillor. But eunuchs and actors did not want Xian at court. Pivot Bureau chief Duan Hui said: "Before the Son of Heaven, if a matter is wrong it can still be corrected. A regional post—if the man is wrong, the harm is no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongtao, campaigning in Shu, said Xian could serve as chief councillor. Eunuchs and actors did not want him at court. Pivot Bureau chief Duan Hui said: "Before the throne, wrong can still be righted. Put the wrong man in a region and the harm is not small.

sentences.zh: 憲材誠可用，不如任以一方。

translations.literal: Xian’s talent is truly usable; better to assign him to a region."
translations.idiomatic: Xian’s talent is real—better give him a command."

sentences.zh: 」乃以為太原尹、北京留守。

translations.literal: He was therefore made governor of Taiyuan and regent of the northern capital.
translations.idiomatic: So he was made governor of Taiyuan and regent of the northern capital.

sentences.zh: 趙在禮作亂，憲家在魏州，在禮善待其家，遣人以書招憲，憲斬其使，不發其書而上之。

translations.literal: Zhao Zaili rebelled. Xian’s family was in Weizhou; Zaili treated them well, sent a man with a letter to recruit Xian, and Xian beheaded the messenger, did not open the letter, and sent it up to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zaili rebelled. Xian’s family was in Weizhou; Zaili treated them kindly and sent a letter to win Xian over. Xian killed the bearer, left the letter sealed, and sent it up.

sentences.zh: 莊宗遇弒，明宗入京師，太原猶未知，而永王存霸奔於太原。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong was murdered. Mingzong entered the capital; Taiyuan did not yet know. Prince of Yong Cunba fled to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong was murdered. Mingzong entered the capital while Taiyuan still did not know. Prince of Yong Cunba fled there.

sentences.zh: 左右告憲曰：「今魏兵南向，主上存亡未可知，存霸之來無詔書，而所乘馬斷其鞦，豈非戰敗者乎！

translations.literal: Those around told Xian: "Wei troops are marching south; the emperor’s life or death is unknown. Cunba came without an imperial edict, and the horse he rode broke its girth—surely a defeated man!
translations.idiomatic: Men around Xian said: "Wei troops march south; the emperor’s fate is unknown. Cunba came without an edict, and his horse broke its girth—a beaten man!

sentences.zh: 宜拘之以俟命。

translations.literal: You should detain him and await orders.
translations.idiomatic: Detain him and wait for word.

sentences.zh: 」憲曰：「吾本書生，無尺寸之功，而人主遇我甚厚，豈有懷二心以幸變，第可與之俱死爾！

translations.literal: " Xian said: "I am a book man by origin, with not a inch of merit, yet my lord treated me with great generosity. How could I harbor a second heart and hope for chaos? I can only die with him!
translations.idiomatic: " Xian said: "I am a scholar by birth with no merit to my name, yet my lord treated me generously. How could I turn traitor and pray for chaos? I can only die with him!

sentences.zh: 」憲從事張昭遠教憲奉表明宗以勸進，憲涕泣拒之。

translations.literal: " Xian’s aide Zhang Zhaoyuan urged Xian to submit a memorial to Mingzong urging enthronement. Xian wept and refused.
translations.idiomatic: " His aide Zhang Zhaoyuan urged him to memorialize Mingzong and press for enthronement. Xian wept and refused.

sentences.zh: 已而存霸削髮，見北京巡檢符彥超，願為僧以求生，彥超麾下兵大噪，殺存霸。

translations.literal: Before long Cunba shaved his head, saw northern-capital inspector Fu Yanchao, and begged to become a monk to save his life. Yanchao’s troops raised a great clamor and killed Cunba.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Cunba shaved his head, sought northern-capital inspector Fu Yanchao, and begged to take the tonsure and live. Yanchao’s soldiers roared and killed him.

sentences.zh: 憲出奔沂州，亦見殺。

translations.literal: Xian fled to Yizhou and was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: Xian fled to Yizhou and was killed as well.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 予於死節之士，得三人而失三人焉。

translations.literal: Among men who died for principle, I have secured three and forfeited three.
translations.idiomatic: Of men who died for principle, I have won three and lost three.

sentences.zh: 鞏廷美、楊溫之死，予既已哀之。

translations.literal: The deaths of Gong Tingmei and Yang Wen I have already mourned.
translations.idiomatic: I have already mourned Gong Tingmei and Yang Wen.

sentences.zh: 至於張憲之事，尤為之痛惜也。

translations.literal: As for Zhang Xian’s affair, I grieve it all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xian’s story grieves me most of all.

sentences.zh: 予於舊史考憲事實，而永王存霸、符彥超與憲傳所書始末皆不同，莫得而考正。

translations.literal: I examined the old histories for the facts of Xian’s case, yet Prince of Yong Cunba, Fu Yanchao, and Xian’s own biography all tell different beginnings and ends—there is no way to verify them.
translations.idiomatic: I searched the old histories for the truth of Xian’s case, but Prince of Yong Cunba, Fu Yanchao, and Xian’s own biography each tell a different story—nothing can be verified.

sentences.zh: 蓋方其變故倉卒之時。

translations.literal: It was simply that in the rush of sudden crisis.
translations.idiomatic: It was simply the rush of sudden crisis.

sentences.zh: 傳者失之爾。

translations.literal: Those who passed the tale on got it wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Those who passed the tale on got it wrong.

sentences.zh: 然要其大節，亦可以見也，憲之志誠可謂忠矣。

translations.literal: Yet grasping the great outline, one can still see it: Xian’s resolve was truly loyal.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the broad outline still shows it—Xian’s resolve was truly loyal.

sentences.zh: 當其不顧其家，絕在禮而斬其使，涕泣以拒昭遠之說，其志甚明。

translations.literal: When he set his household aside, broke with Zaili and executed his envoy, and wept as he refused Zhaoyuan’s counsel, his purpose was plain.
translations.idiomatic: He set his household aside, broke with Zaili and killed his envoy, and wept as he refused Zhaoyuan’s counsel—his purpose was plain.

sentences.zh: 至其欲與存霸俱死，及存霸被殺，反棄太原而出奔，然猶不知其心果欲何為也。

translations.literal: When he wished to die with Cunba, and after Cunba was killed instead abandoned Taiyuan and fled, one still cannot know what his heart truly meant to do.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to die with Cunba; when Cunba was killed he abandoned Taiyuan and fled—what his heart truly meant, no one can say.

sentences.zh: 而舊史書憲坐棄城而賜死，予亦以為不然。

translations.literal: The old histories say Xian was put to death for abandoning the city; I too hold that wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The old histories say Xian was executed for abandoning the city; I hold that wrong.

sentences.zh: 予之於憲固欲成其美誌，而要在憲失其官守而其死不明，故不得列於死節也。

translations.literal: I indeed wished to complete a fine record for Xian, but the point is that Xian lost his post and his death is unclear—so he cannot be listed among those who died for principle.
translations.idiomatic: I wished to honor Xian with a fine record, but he lost his post and his death is unclear—he cannot stand among those who died for principle.

sentences.zh: 蕭希甫

translations.literal: Xiao Xifu
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xifu

sentences.zh: 蕭希甫，宋州人也。

translations.literal: Xiao Xifu was a native of Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xifu came from Song Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 為人有機辯，多矯激，少舉進士，為梁開封尹袁象先掌書記。

translations.literal: As a man he was quick-witted and disputatious, given to extravagant provocation. In youth he passed the jinshi examination and served Liang’s Kaifeng governor Yuan Xiangxian as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and disputatious, prone to extravagant provocation, he passed the jinshi in youth and served Liang’s Kaifeng governor Yuan Xiangxian as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 象先為青州節度使，以希甫為巡官。

translations.literal: When Xiangxian became military governor of Qingzhou, he made Xifu a circuit inspector.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiangxian became military governor of Qingzhou, he made Xifu a circuit inspector.

sentences.zh: 希甫不樂，乃棄其母妻，變姓名，亡之鎮州，自稱青州掌書記，謁趙王王镕。

translations.literal: Xifu was displeased. He abandoned his mother and wife, changed his name, and fled to Zhen Prefecture, calling himself chief secretary of Qingzhou and presenting himself to the Zhao king Wang Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Xifu was displeased. He abandoned mother and wife, changed his name, and fled to Zhen Prefecture, posing as Qingzhou’s chief secretary to gain audience with Wang Rong of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 镕以希甫為參軍，尤不樂，居歲餘，又亡之易州，削髮為僧，居百丈山。

translations.literal: Rong made Xifu a staff officer; he was still more unhappy. After more than a year he fled again to Yi Prefecture, shaved his head, became a monk, and lived on Mount Baizhang.
translations.idiomatic: Rong made him a staff officer; he liked it even less. A year later he fled to Yi Prefecture, shaved his head, and became a monk on Mount Baizhang.

sentences.zh: 莊宗將建國於魏，置百官，求天下隱逸之士，幽州李紹宏薦希甫為魏州推官。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong was about to establish his state at Wei, set up the hundred offices, and seek hidden worthies throughout the realm, Youzhou’s Li Shaohong recommended Xifu as Wei Prefecture’s legal officer.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhuangzong prepared to found his state at Wei, fill the hundred offices, and seek hidden worthies, Li Shaohong of Youzhou recommended Xifu as legal officer at Wei.

sentences.zh: 莊宗即帝位，欲以知制誥，有詔定內宴儀，問希甫：「樞密使得坐否？

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne he wished to make Xifu drafter of edicts. An edict was issued to fix the rites of inner banquets, and Xifu was asked: “May the Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner be seated?
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong took the throne he meant to make Xifu drafter of edicts. An edict fixed the rites of inner banquets, and Xifu was asked: “May the Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner be seated?

sentences.zh: 」希甫以為不可。

translations.literal: ” Xifu said it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: ” Xifu said no.

sentences.zh: 樞密使張居翰聞之怒，謂希甫曰：「老夫歷事三朝天子，見內宴數百，子本田舍兒，安知宮禁事？

translations.literal: Bureau commissioner Zhang Juhuan heard and was furious. He told Xifu: “This old man has served three dynasties and seen hundreds of inner banquets. You were a farm boy—what do you know of palace affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Zhang Juhuan heard and was furious. He told Xifu: “I have served three dynasties and seen hundreds of inner banquets. You were a farm boy—what do you know of palace affairs?

sentences.zh: 」希甫不能對。

translations.literal: ” Xifu could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: ” Xifu had no reply.

sentences.zh: 由是宦官用事者皆切齒。

translations.literal: From this the eunuchs in power all gnashed their teeth at him.
translations.idiomatic: From this every eunuch in power gnashed his teeth at him.

sentences.zh: 宰相豆盧革等希宦官旨，共排斥之，以為駕部郎中，希甫失誌，尤怏怏。

translations.literal: Chief councillors Dou Luge and the others, courting the eunuchs’ favor, joined in driving him out and made him director in the Department of Imperial Transport. Xifu lost his aim and grew still more sullen.
translations.idiomatic: Chief councillors Dou Luge and the rest, courting the eunuchs, joined in driving him out and made him director in the Department of Imperial Transport. Xifu lost his aim and grew sullen.

sentences.zh: 莊宗滅梁，遣希甫宣慰青齊，希甫始知其母已死，而妻袁氏亦改嫁矣。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong destroyed Liang he sent Xifu to console Qing and Qi. Only then did Xifu learn his mother was already dead and his wife, the Yuan clan, had remarried.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong destroyed Liang he sent Xifu to console Qing and Qi. Only then did Xifu learn his mother was dead and his wife, Lady Yuan, had remarried.

sentences.zh: 希甫乃發哀服喪，居於魏州，人有引漢李陵書以譏之曰：「老母終堂，生妻去室。

translations.literal: Xifu then put on mourning and observed the rites, living at Wei Prefecture. Someone quoted Han Li Ling’s letter to mock him: “My old mother still in the hall; my living wife has left the house.
translations.idiomatic: Xifu put on mourning and observed the rites at Wei. Someone quoted Li Ling’s letter to mock him: “My old mother still in the hall; my living wife has left the house.

sentences.zh: 」時皆傳以為笑。

translations.literal: ” At the time all passed it around as a joke.
translations.idiomatic: ” Everyone passed it around as a joke.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，召為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, Xifu was summoned as Remonstrating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne, Xifu was summoned as Remonstrating Censor.

sentences.zh: 是時，復置匭函，以希甫為使，希甫建言：「自兵亂相乘，王綱大壞，侵欺淩奪，有力者勝。

translations.literal: At that time the petition box was restored, and Xifu was made its commissioner. Xifu proposed: “Since war and rebellion have followed one upon another, the royal norms are greatly broken, and seizure, oppression, and plunder go to the strong.
translations.idiomatic: The petition box was restored and Xifu was made its commissioner. He proposed: “War and rebellion have followed one upon another; royal norms lie in ruins; seizure and plunder go to the strong.

sentences.zh: 凡略人之妻女，占人之田宅，奸臟之吏，刑獄之冤者，何可勝紀？

translations.literal: Men who seize others’ wives and daughters, occupy others’ fields and houses, corrupt officials, and those wronged in the prisons—how can they all be counted?
