translations.idiomatic: Men who seize wives and daughters, occupy fields and houses, corrupt officials, prisoners wronged in the courts—who could count them all?

sentences.zh: 而匭函一出，投訴必多，至於功臣貴戚，有不得繩之以法者。

translations.literal: Yet once the petition box appears, complaints will surely flood in—even meritorious ministers and imperial kin may not be bound by law.
translations.idiomatic: Yet once the petition box appears, complaints will flood in—even meritorious ministers and imperial kin may escape the law.

sentences.zh: 」乃自天成元年四月二十八日昧爽已前，大辟已上，皆赦除之，然後出匭函以示眾。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon, before dawn on the twenty-eighth day of the fourth month of the first year of Tiancheng, all capital crimes and above were pardoned and cleared; only then was the petition box opened to the people.
translations.idiomatic: ” Before dawn on the twenty-eighth day of the fourth month of Tiancheng 1, all capital crimes and above were pardoned; only then was the petition box opened to the people.

sentences.zh: 初，明宗欲以希甫為諫議大夫，豆盧革、韋說頗沮難之。

translations.literal: At first, when Mingzong wished to make Xifu Remonstrating Censor, Dou Luge and Wei Shuo strongly obstructed it.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Mingzong wished to make Xifu Remonstrating Censor, Dou Luge and Wei Shuo strongly obstructed it.

sentences.zh: 其後革、說為安重誨所惡，希甫希旨，誣奏：「革縱田客殺人，而說與鄰人爭井，井有寶貨。

translations.literal: Later, when Ge and Shuo were hated by An Chonghui, Xifu courted the throne’s intent and falsely memorialized: “Ge let his tenant farmers kill men, and Shuo quarreled with a neighbor over a well said to hold treasure.
translations.idiomatic: Later Ge and Shuo fell under An Chonghui’s hatred. Xifu courted the throne and falsely memorialized: “Ge let tenant farmers kill men; Shuo quarreled with a neighbor over a well said to hold treasure.

sentences.zh: 」有司推劾，井中惟破釜而已，革、說終皆貶死。

translations.literal: ” The offices investigated; in the well there was only a broken cauldron. In the end Ge and Shuo were both demoted and died.
translations.idiomatic: ” The offices investigated; the well held only a broken cauldron. Ge and Shuo were demoted and died.

sentences.zh: 明宗賜希甫帛百匹、粟麥三百石，拜左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Mingzong rewarded Xifu with a hundred bolts of silk and three hundred shi of grain and wheat, and appointed him Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong rewarded Xifu with a hundred bolts of silk and three hundred shi of grain and wheat, and made him Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 希甫性褊而躁進，嘗遣人夜叩宮門上變，言河堰牙官李筠告本軍謀反，詰旦，追問無狀，斬筠，軍士詣安重誨求希甫啖之。

translations.literal: Xifu was narrow-minded and eager to advance. Once he sent a man by night to knock at the palace gate and report an emergency, saying the river-dam petty officer Li Jun had denounced his army for plotting rebellion. At dawn, when the case was pursued, there was no substance; Jun was beheaded, and the soldiers went to An Chonghui demanding Xifu’s flesh to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Xifu was narrow-minded and eager to advance. Once he sent a man by night to knock at the palace gate and report an emergency: river-dam officer Li Jun had denounced his army for plotting rebellion. At dawn the charge proved empty; Jun was beheaded, and the soldiers went to An Chonghui demanding Xifu’s flesh.

sentences.zh: 是時，明宗將有事於南郊，前齋一日，群臣習儀於殿廷，宰相馮道、趙鳳，河南尹秦王從榮，樞密使安重誨候班於月華門外。

translations.literal: At that time Mingzong was about to perform the southern suburban rites. On the day before the preliminary fast, the ministers rehearsed the ceremony in the hall. Chief councillors Feng Dao and Zhao Feng, Henan governor Prince of Qin Congrong, and Bureau commissioner An Chonghui waited in formation outside the Moon Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong was about to perform the southern suburban rites. On the eve of the preliminary fast the ministers rehearsed in the hall. Chief councillors Feng Dao and Zhao Feng, Henan governor Prince of Qin Congrong, and Bureau commissioner An Chonghui waited in formation outside the Moon Gate.

sentences.zh: 希甫與兩省班先入，道等坐廓下不起，既出，希甫召堂頭直省朝堂驅使官，責問宰相、樞密見兩省官何得不起，因大詬詈。

translations.literal: Xifu entered first with the two departments’ ranks. Dao and the others sat in the corridor and did not rise. After they came out, Xifu summoned the head attendant of the direct palace secretariat hall ushers and rebuked him: why had the chief councillors and Bureau commissioner not risen when they saw officials of the two departments? Then he cursed them savagely.
translations.idiomatic: Xifu entered first with the two departments’ ranks. Dao and the others sat in the corridor and did not rise. When they came out, Xifu summoned the head hall usher and demanded why chief councillors and the Bureau commissioner had not risen before officials of the two departments—then cursed them savagely.

sentences.zh: 是夜，托疾還第。

translations.literal: That night he pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: That night he pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 月余，坐告李筠事動搖軍眾，貶嵐州司戶參軍，卒於貶所。

translations.literal: More than a month later, on the charge that his report about Li Jun had shaken the army, he was demoted to Lanzhou revenue assistant and died in exile.
translations.idiomatic: A month later, charged with shaking the army by his report on Li Jun, he was demoted to Lanzhou revenue assistant and died in exile.

sentences.zh: 劉贊，魏州人也。

translations.literal: Liu Zan was a native of Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zan came from Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父比為縣令，贊始就學，衣以青布衫襦，每食則比自肉食，而別以蔬食食贊於床下，謂之曰：「肉食，君之祿也，爾欲之，則勤學問以幹祿；

translations.literal: His father Bi had been a county magistrate. When Zan first began his studies, Bi clothed him in a blue cloth jacket and trousers. At each meal Bi ate meat himself and set vegetables apart to feed Zan beneath the bed, telling him: “Meat is the ruler’s stipend. If you want it, study hard to win office through merit;
translations.idiomatic: His father Bi had been a county magistrate. When Zan first studied, Bi dressed him in blue cloth jacket and trousers. At each meal Bi ate meat himself and fed Zan vegetables beneath the bed, saying: “Meat is the ruler’s stipend. If you want it, study hard and win office through merit;

sentences.zh: 吾肉非爾之食也。

translations.literal: My meat is not food for you.
translations.idiomatic: My meat is not food for you.

sentences.zh: 」由是贊益力學，舉進士，為羅紹威判官，去為租庸使趙巖巡官，又為孔謙鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: ” From this Zan studied all the harder, passed the jinshi, and served Luo Shaowei as adjutant. He left to become an inspector under grain-and-corvée commissioner Zhao Yan, then salt-and-iron adjutant under Kong Qian.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zan studied harder, passed the jinshi, and served Luo Shaowei as adjutant. He left to inspect under grain-and-corvée commissioner Zhao Yan, then became salt-and-iron adjutant under Kong Qian.

sentences.zh: 明宗時，累遷中書舍人、御史中丞、刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Under Mingzong he rose in succession to Secretariat drafter, censor-in-chief, and vice minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingzong he rose to Secretariat drafter, censor-in-chief, and vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 守官以法，權豪不可幹以私。

translations.literal: He held office by the law; the powerful could not sway him with private favor.
translations.idiomatic: He held office by the law; the powerful could not sway him with private favor.

sentences.zh: 是時，秦王從榮握兵而驕，多過失，言事者請置師傅以輔道之。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Qin Congrong held troops and was arrogant, with many faults. Memorialists asked that a tutor be appointed to guide him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qin Congrong held troops, grew arrogant, and piled up faults. Memorialists asked that a tutor be appointed to guide him.

sentences.zh: 大臣畏王，不敢決其事，因請王得自擇，秦王即請贊，乃拜贊秘書監，為秦王傅。

translations.literal: The great ministers feared the prince and dared not decide the matter, so they asked that the prince choose for himself. The prince at once named Zan, and Zan was appointed Director of the Secretariat and tutor to the prince.
translations.idiomatic: The great ministers feared the prince and dared not decide, so they let him choose. Congrong named Zan at once; Zan was made Director of the Secretariat and tutor to the prince.

sentences.zh: 贊泣曰：「禍將至矣！

translations.literal: Zan wept and said: “Disaster is coming!
translations.idiomatic: Zan wept: “Disaster is coming!

sentences.zh: 」秦王所請王府元帥官屬十餘人，類多浮薄傾險之徒，日獻諛諂以驕王，獨贊從容諷諫，率以正道。

translations.literal: ” More than ten staff officers the prince had requested for his princely headquarters were mostly frivolous and treacherous men who daily offered flattery to puff up the prince. Only Zan, at ease, offered indirect remonstrance, always by the upright path.
translations.idiomatic: ” More than ten staff officers Congrong had chosen for his princely headquarters were mostly frivolous, treacherous men who daily flattered him to puff up his pride. Only Zan, at ease, offered indirect remonstrance along the upright path.

sentences.zh: 秦王嘗命賓客作文於坐中，贊自以師傅，恥與群小比伍，雖操筆勉強，有不悅之色。

translations.literal: Once the prince ordered his guests to compose essays in his presence. Zan, taking himself for tutor, was ashamed to rank with the petty men; though he took up the brush with effort, his face showed displeasure.
translations.idiomatic: Once the prince ordered his guests to compose essays before him. Zan, as tutor, was ashamed to rank with petty men; though he wrote, his face showed displeasure.

sentences.zh: 秦王惡之，後戒左右贊來不得通，贊亦不往，月一至府而已，退則杜門不交人事。

translations.literal: The prince hated him. Later he warned his attendants not to admit Zan; Zan stopped coming, visiting the princely residence only once a month. In retirement he shut his doors and kept out of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The prince hated him. He warned his attendants not to admit Zan; Zan stopped coming, visiting only once a month. In retirement he shut his doors and kept out of affairs.

sentences.zh: 已而秦王果敗死，唐大臣議王屬官當坐者，馮道曰：「元帥判官任贊與秦王非素好，而在職不逾月，詹事王居敏及劉贊皆以正直為王所惡，河南府判官司徒詡病告家居久，皆宜不與其謀。

translations.literal: Before long the prince indeed fell and died. Tang’s great ministers debated which of the prince’s staff should be punished. Feng Dao said: “Marshal adjutant Ren Zan was no old friend of the prince and served less than a month. Household tutor Wang Jumin and Liu Zan were both hated by the prince for their uprightness. Henan prefectural adjutant Situ Xu had long been on sick leave at home. None should be charged with plotting.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the prince fell and died. Tang’s great ministers debated punishment for his staff. Feng Dao said: “Marshal adjutant Ren Zan was no old friend of the prince and served less than a month. Household tutor Wang Jumin and Liu Zan were hated for their uprightness. Henan adjutant Situ Xu had long been on sick leave. None should be charged with plotting.

sentences.zh: 而諮議參軍高輦與王最厚，輦法當死，其餘可次第原減。

translations.literal: Advisory aide Gao Nian was closest to the prince; by law Nian should die, and the rest may be reduced in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Advisory aide Gao Nian was closest to the prince; by law he should die, and the rest may be reduced in turn.

sentences.zh: 」朱弘昭曰：「諸公不知其意爾，使秦王得入光政門，當待贊等如何？

translations.literal: ” Zhu Hongzhao said: “You gentlemen do not know his mind. If the prince had entered the Guangzheng Gate, what would he have done with Zan and the rest?
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhu Hongzhao said: “You do not know his mind. If the prince had entered Guangzheng Gate, what would he have done with Zan and the rest?

sentences.zh: 吾徒復有家族邪！

translations.literal: Would any of us still have had our families!
translations.idiomatic: Would any of us still have had families!

sentences.zh: 且法有首從，今秦王夫婦男女皆死，而贊等止其一身幸矣！

translations.literal: Moreover the law distinguishes leaders from followers. Now the prince, his wife, sons, and daughters are all dead, and Zan and the rest keep only their own lives—that is already fortune!
translations.idiomatic: The law distinguishes leaders from followers. The prince, his wife, sons, and daughters are all dead—Zan and the rest keeping their lives is already fortune!

sentences.zh: 」道等難之。

translations.literal: ” Dao and the others found it hard to answer.
translations.idiomatic: ” Dao and the others had no answer.

sentences.zh: 而馮赟亦爭不可，贊等乃免死。

translations.literal: Feng Yun also argued it could not be done, and Zan and the rest were spared death.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yun also argued against it, and Zan and the rest were spared death.

sentences.zh: 於是論高輦死，而任贊等十七人皆長流。

translations.literal: Thereupon Gao Nian was sentenced to death, and Ren Zan and seventeen others were all sent into long exile.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Nian was sentenced to death; Ren Zan and seventeen others were sent into long exile.

sentences.zh: 初，贊聞秦王敗，即白衣駕驢以俟，人有告贊奪官而已，贊曰：「豈有天子冢嗣見殺，而賓僚奪官者乎，不死幸矣！

translations.literal: At first, when Zan heard the prince had fallen, he put on plain clothes and drove a donkey to wait. Someone told him Zan would only lose his office. Zan said: “Can it be that the heir of the Son of Heaven was killed, yet his staff merely lose their posts? Not to die is already fortune!
translations.idiomatic: When Zan heard the prince had fallen, he put on plain clothes and drove a donkey to wait. Someone told him he would only lose office. Zan said: “The heir of the Son of Heaven was killed—can his staff merely lose their posts? Not to die is already fortune!

sentences.zh: 」已而贊長流嵐州百姓。

translations.literal: ” In the end Zan was long exiled as a commoner of Lan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: ” In the end Zan was long exiled to Lan Prefecture as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 清泰二年，詔歸田里，行至石會關，病卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qingtai an edict recalled him to his home district. On the road at Shihui Pass he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingtai 2 an edict recalled him home. On the road at Shihui Pass he fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 何瓚，閩人也，唐末舉進士及第。

translations.literal: He Zan was a native of Min. At the end of Tang he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He Zan came from Min. At the end of Tang he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 莊宗為太原節度使，辟為判官。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong was military governor of Taiyuan, he recruited Zan as adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong was military governor of Taiyuan, he recruited Zan as adjutant.

sentences.zh: 莊宗每出征伐，留張承業守太原，承業卒，瓚代知留守事。

translations.literal: Whenever Zhuangzong marched on campaign he left Zhang Chengye to hold Taiyuan. When Chengye died, Zan took charge of the regency in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Zhuangzong marched on campaign he left Zhang Chengye at Taiyuan. When Chengye died, Zan took charge of the regency.

sentences.zh: 瓚為人明敏，通於吏事，外若疏簡而內頗周密。

translations.literal: Zan was bright and quick, skilled in administrative affairs; outwardly he seemed loose and simple, inwardly he was quite thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Zan was bright and quick, skilled in administration; outwardly loose and simple, inwardly thorough.

sentences.zh: 莊宗建大號於鄴都，拜瓚諫議大夫，瓚慮莊宗事不成，求留守北京。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong established his great title at Ye, he appointed Zan Remonstrating Censor. Zan feared Zhuangzong’s cause might fail and asked to remain regent of the northern capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong established his great title at Ye, he made Zan Remonstrating Censor. Zan feared Zhuangzong’s cause might fail and asked to remain regent of the northern capital.

sentences.zh: 瓚與明宗有舊，明宗即位，召還，見於內殿，勞問久之，已而以瓚為西川節度副使。

translations.literal: Zan was old friends with Mingzong. When Mingzong took the throne he summoned him back, received him in the inner hall, and questioned him at length before appointing him deputy military governor of Xichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zan was old friends with Mingzong. When Mingzong took the throne he summoned him back, received him in the inner hall, questioned him at length, and made him deputy military governor of Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 是時，孟知祥已有二誌，方以副使趙季良為心腹，聞瓚代之，亟奏留季良，遂改瓚行軍司馬。

translations.literal: At that time Meng Zhixiang already had two minds; he had just made deputy governor Zhao Jiliang his confidant. Hearing Zan would replace him, he urgently memorialized to keep Jiliang and had Zan made army campaign aide instead.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang already had two minds and had made deputy governor Zhao Jiliang his confidant. Hearing Zan would replace him, he urgently memorialized to keep Jiliang and had Zan made army campaign aide instead.

sentences.zh: 瓚恥於自辭，不得已而往，明宗賜予甚厚。

translations.literal: Zan was ashamed to decline himself and went against his will. Mingzong rewarded him richly.
translations.idiomatic: Zan was ashamed to decline and went against his will. Mingzong rewarded him richly.

sentences.zh: 初，知祥在北京為馬步軍都虞候，而瓚留守太原，知祥以軍禮事瓚，瓚常繩以法，知祥初不樂，及瓚為司馬，猶勉待之甚厚。

translations.literal: At first, when Zhixiang was chief inspector of horse and foot at the northern capital and Zan held Taiyuan as regent, Zhixiang treated Zan with military courtesy. Zan often bound him by law. Zhixiang was displeased at first; when Zan became campaign aide, he still treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zhixiang was chief inspector of horse and foot at the northern capital while Zan held Taiyuan as regent. Zhixiang treated him with military courtesy; Zan often bound him by law. Zhixiang was displeased at first; when Zan became campaign aide, he still treated him generously.

sentences.zh: 知祥反，罷瓚司馬，置之私第，瓚飲恨而卒。

translations.literal: When Zhixiang rebelled he removed Zan as campaign aide, kept him in a private residence, and Zan died nursing his grievance.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhixiang rebelled he stripped Zan of his post as campaign aide, kept him in a private residence, and Zan died nursing his grievance.
